parsed.explanation: The text defines v(B) via the fixed decreasing order b_1≥⋯≥b_r. Lemma 4.1 yields only SOME ordering of P∪N with nested difference g, and nested difference is order-dependent. The witness checks out: for {8,7,6,5,4}, decreasing order gives ||||8−7|−6|−5|−4| = 4, while the Lemma-4.1 greedy ordering 8,6,5,7,4 (P={8,7}, N={6,5,4}, both sums 15) gives 0. So 'some ordering has value g' does not imply the decreasing-order v(P∪N)≤S/(2^m−1); Theorem 4.2, as stated, is unproved. Moreover the strategy explicitly takes B={b_1≥⋯≥b_r}, processes b_2,…,b_r in that decreasing order, and equates the leftover with v(B), so the achieved D is exactly the unbounded decreasing-order value. No other passage repairs this; the two-line fix (process in the greedy order) is not written. Upper bound invalid as written.
